text.p: These are the leading stories in the Pakistani press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
THE NEWS
- The government has prepared a case against former prime minister Benazir Bhutto for alleged irregularities in the sale of Kot Addu power station.
- Opposition leader Benazir Bhutto demanded that a judicial commission should be set up to review all the deals of the Privatisation Commission.
THE MUSLIM
- Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif vowed to enforce an effective justice system in the country in line with Sharia (Islamic law) to ensure immediate punishment for criminals.
- Thousands of people attended the funeral of renowned Pakistan singer Nusrat Fateh Ali Khan who died of a heart attack in London on Saturday.
THE NATION
- The opposition Pakistan People's Party is planning to launch a protest campaign against the government.
- Chief of Tehrik-i-Jafria Pakistan (TJP) Allama Sajid Naqvi was arrested by police in Lahore on Sunday.
DAWN
- President Farooq Leghari signed the Anti-Terrorism Bill, 1997 into an Act. A senior government official said speedy trial courts would be set up this month in line with the law.
- Two people were killed and two others wounded when two unidentified gunmen opened fire at a musical show in Karachi organised to mark the golden jubilee celebrations.
- The prime ministers of India, Pakistan and Bangladesh are expected to head business delegations at a special meeting in Dhaka later this year, an Indian diplomat said.
BUSINESS RECORDER

- The government is the biggest beneficiary of falling lending rates as it retired 40 billion rupees in loans taken at 17.5 percent by raising fresh loans at 15.5 percent or less, resulting in an improvement in cash balances.
- The Pakistan Telecommunication Co Ltd may implement rate cuts on its settlement charges with U.S. telephone companies after June 1998, which would hit its revenues.
- The World Bank said Pakistan's new fiscal policies for the oil and gas sector were better than those of other South Asian countries.
- The government rejected a renewed request by the Water and Power Development Authority for power tariff increases.
- Due to financial stringency, the Agriculture Development Bank of Pakistan has asked local manufacturers to supply tractors to farmers on five-month credit.
- The death anniversary of president General Mohammad Zia-ul-Haq was observed in Islamabad.
- Tax changes have reduced the profitability of modarabas (Islamic mutual funds) as exemptions were given only to mutual funds and unit trusts, ignoring the Islamic finance system.
- The Punjab provincial government has constituted a Cabinet Committee on privatisation to oversee the activities of the Punjab Privatisation Board.
